papers.title: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
papers.abstract: Objective: Conventional microelectrode arrays (MEAs) are suboptimal for long-term electrophysiology of three-dimensional (3D) excitable tissues, as limited oxygenation, nutrient diffusion, and tissue-electrode coupling compromise recording stability. Air-liquid interface (ALI) culture mitigates these constraints, but existing ALI MEA platforms are limited in channel count, flexibility, and compatibility with commercial multichannel acquisition systems. We developed and comprehensively characterized a next-generation ALI MEA for standardized, long-term recordings across multiple 3D excitable tissue models. Approach: The novel ALI MEA60 is composed of a porous polyimide membrane that integrates an array of 60 thin film microelectrodes (59 recording, one reference) and a basal perfusion chamber with Luer-lock connectors for controlled medium exchange and pharmacological wash-in/wash-out. It is compatible with the MEA2100-Mini data acquisition system (Multi Channel Systems). We characterized electrode impedance and noise across 41 ALI MEA60 devices, assessed 60-day stability with human iPSC-derived neural spheroids (N = 7 MEAs, 121 recordings) using a standardized longitudinal framework and linear mixed-effects models, and evaluated its versatility through pharmacological assays and recordings from human neural spheroids, brain organoids, ex vivo brain slices, and cardiac organoids. Main results: The platform showed reproducible electrical performance (median impedance 56 kOhms; at 1 kHz) and low noise (approx. 5uV Root Mean Square (RMS) in saline, 10-20 uV in medium), resolving spikes and local field potentials simultaneously. Recording remained stable for at least 60 days, with a stable noise floor and ~85% persistence of initial functional channels. Neural spheroids reproduced the standard qualitative signatures to gabazine, 4-aminopyridine (4-AP), and 6-Cyano-7-nitroquinoxaline-2,3-dione/D-2-amino-5-phosphonovalerate (CNQX/D-AP5), while cardiac organoids showed the expected beta-adrenergic response to isoproterenol. The ALI MEA60 can similarly record signals from human brain slices and organoids without hardware modification. Significance: The ALI MEA60 combines ALI culture, chronic recording stability, standardized pharmacological testing and cross-tissue compatibility in a single ready-to-use platform. It also establishes a reproducible framework for benchmarking long-term electrophysiological performance, thereby supporting disease modelling, drug discovery, organ-on-chip technologies and future chronic 3D electrophysiology systems. Keywords: microelectrode array (MEA); air-liquid interface (ALI); 3D excitable tissues; neural spheroids; cardiac organoids; chronic electrophysiology.

papers.title: Neural processing of linguistic speech features and their modulation by selective attention in users of hearing aids and cochlear implants
papers.abstract: Understanding speech relies on the neural processing of acoustic and linguistic features, which can both be analyzed using Temporal Response Functions (TRFs). While both types of features have been the focus of numerous studies in typical-hearing individuals, much less is known about the neural processing of continuous speech for people with hearing loss, particularly how hearing-impaired listeners process word-level features in noisy environments, where they typically struggle. We recorded EEG from hearing aid (HA, n=29) and cochlear implant (CI, n=24) users, and an age-matched typical-hearing (TH) control group (n=29), while participants listened to audiobook segments in quiet and with a competing speaker, using their personal hearing devices (CI and HA). A hierarchical encoding framework incrementally added word onset, word frequency, and word surprisal as predictors of the EEG signal. Attentional modulation was assessed by comparing encoding scores for attended versus ignored speech. All three groups showed clear neural responses to word onset, frequency, and surprisal for speech in quiet. Surprisal tracking emerged at 400~ms in TH participants, 500~ms in HA users, and 600~ms in CI users, weakest in the CI group. All three groups exhibited attentional modulation of surprisal tracking. Word frequency yielded significant encoding gains in quiet only for TH and HI listeners, not CI users. We show for the first time that CI users exhibit significant, attention-modulated neural responses to word surprisal. More broadly, surprisal tracking was present across all hearing-impaired groups but weakest in CI users, the cohort with the greatest difficulty understanding speech in noise.

papers.title: Electrophysiological correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of pain
papers.abstract: Positive and negative expectations can substantially shape pain and analgesic treatment outcomes, highlighting the need to elucidate neural mechanisms underlying placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia. The primary aim of this feasibility study was to assess adaptations to an established placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm in the context of electroencephalography (EEG). The secondary aim was to assess EEG correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of experimental heat pain in healthy volunteers. Placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia were induced in a within-subjects design in 20 young adults through verbal instructions, a conditioning procedure and (sham) transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation while EEG was recorded. Placebo and nocebo effects as well as positive and negative pain expectations were successfully established, demonstrating paradigm effectiveness. EEG results showed increased theta, alpha and beta power in the placebo compared to the control condition during pain delivery, and in the nocebo compared to the control condition during pain anticipation and delivery. Additionally, gamma-band power was increased in the nocebo compared to the placebo condition as a function of a higher perceived pain intensity. Taken together, feasibility of the EEG-compatible placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm was demonstrated. Furthermore, our EEG results are in line with previous findings that, in the context of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia, link theta-, alpha- and beta-band activity to top-down processing, and gamma-band activity to expectation-modulated sensory processing.

papers.title: Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridging Network for Motor Execution to Motor Imagery EEG Transfer in Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) hold promising application prospects in the fields of limb motor rehabilitation and human-computer interaction. However, the reliability of MI calibration data is limited by the difficulty of verifying participants' engagement during motor imagerywhereas motor execution (ME) provides a more readily supervised source of motor-related information.To investigate the potential of ME-derived knowledge for assisting MI decoding, we propose a Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridge Network (SE-RTBNet) to achieve accurate intra-subject cross-task knowledge transfer from ME to MI. The proposed framework consists of two major components: a shared encoder and a residual task-bridge module. The shared encoder extracts stable general motor representations from multi-band EEG signals and explores the shared feature patterns underlying ME and MI tasks. The residual task-bridge module is equipped with a performance-aware routing mechanism. It adaptively compensates for task-specific discrepancies between the two tasks, enabling precise cross-task feature alignment and knowledge transfer. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, experiments are conducted on three public datasets. The proposed method achieves average classification accuracies of 69.39%, 74.61%, and 98.94%, respectively, and outperforms existing transfer-learning algorithms in overall performance. Our model provides an effective strategy for reducing dependence on extensive MI calibration data through intra-subject cross-task knowledge transfer.The source code of the proposed SE-RTBNet is publicly available at https://github.com/Daisyzyx2002/SE-RTBNet

papers.title: Differential routing of spectral light inputs redistributes circadian phase sensitivity
papers.abstract: Shared sensory channels create a routing problem when biological functions require different combinations of the same environmental inputs. In phototrophic systems, spectral light signals can influence both circadian entrainment and irradiance-dependent physiology. We formulate a two-channel framework that separates common changes in channel activity from differential changes in their relative balance and asks how a locked oscillator represents these directions. Input routing and entrainment stability are inseparable in the locked state: common and differential sensitivities depend on signed, cycle-averaged pathway projections together with the local stiffness of locking. Temporal gating provides one constructive route to a differential projection because two positive pathways can weight opposite-signed regions of a phase-response curve at different times. A canonical repressilator establishes feasibility, while a distinct zeitgeber-gated nonlinear implementation reproduces the same qualitative directional hierarchy. A prescribed positive physiological projection shows that irradiance responsiveness can remain available to a second output. The resulting principle is a redistribution of sensitivity across input directions rather than global attenuation, with experimentally testable predictions for shared multichannel sensing.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.abstract: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges. We analysed electroencephalography from 1,534 participants aged 5 to 21 years in the Healthy Brain Network during a contrast-change discrimination task. On the same trials, we measured the visual response and an evidence-accumulation signal, while a decision model estimated accumulation efficiency, attention lapses and non-decision time. We found that the visual response did not grow with age and retained 77% of its strength on missed targets. Instead, accuracy improved through fewer lapses and more efficient accumulation, both reaching half of their developmental change by about 9 years, whereas speed improved later: non-decision time shortened between 11 and 14 years and was longer in children whose accumulation signal rose later. These findings show that perceptual decision-making matures through dissociable stages rather than a single global increase in processing speed: mechanisms supporting accuracy mature in middle childhood, whereas those supporting the fastest responses continue to develop into early adolescence. This framework links developmental theories of processing speed to neural mechanisms of decision-making and provides a reference for identifying which component is disrupted in children who struggle.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

papers.title: Precision of sensory representations in cortex is indexed by alpha power and pupil dilation, and tracks the dynamics of correlated noise
papers.abstract: Sensory representations fluctuate in precision from moment to moment, shaping the fidelity of perception and memory. Population-coding theory proposes that these fluctuations are constrained by correlated variability within neural populations, yet linking these mechanisms to behaviour and brain state in humans has remained challenging. Here we combined EEG with an encoding-decoding framework to reconstruct orientation-selective population responses and quantify representational precision dynamically over time. Precision predicted subsequent working-memory performance and evolved in close correspondence with the dynamics of correlated variability between decoded orientation channels. Following stimulus onset, correlated variability was selectively suppressed among similarly tuned channels, the pattern predicted to maximise coding fidelity. Prestimulus alpha power and pupil size independently predicted representational precision, linking these dynamics to endogenous cortical and neuromodulatory state. Together, these findings identify candidate mechanisms and accessible physiological markers of representational precision in humans.

papers.title: ProlateNet: Sampling-rate transfer of convolutional networks with a weights-only certificate for physiological signals
papers.abstract: A central goal of physiological signal analysis is to train a model once and deploy it across recording systems. However, these systems sample EEG and ECG at different rates, and a network trained at one rate loses accuracy at the others. Continuous-kernel networks were built to solve this problem, but published ones still fail at unseen rates, and no existing method can certify a trained model before deployment. In this study, we propose ProlateNet, which builds kernels from prolate spheroidal wave functions to suppress aliasing across sampling rates and certifies a trained model from its weights alone. Across fourteen first-layer designs trained at one rate on three public EEG and ECG datasets, the published continuous-kernel layers FlexConv and sampling-frequency-independent (SFI) convolution show mean worst drops of 0.18 and 0.35 macro-F1 on SEED. ProlateNet is the only design that is stable and accurate on all three datasets with an error bound fixed before training, and its mean worst drop is at most 0.003. Without target-rate recordings, its certificate ranks the continuous-kernel designs on SEED by measured transfer with Spearman {rho} = 0.92, against 0.68 for energy above the training Nyquist frequency. Overall, ProlateNet shows that controlling aliasing enables convolutional networks to transfer across sampling rates and provides principled guidance for building physiological signal models that are trained once and deployed across recording systems.

papers.title: Dissociable patterns of neurophysiological alterations during guided search in schizophrenia and autism: Evidence from fixation-related potentials, alpha modulation, and functional MRI.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia (SZ) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are associated with convergent differences in social perception relative to non-autistic, non-schizophrenia controls (NC), but divergent patterns of alterations in early visual activity. Here, we used multimodal imaging during the Guided Visual Search task to investigate the differential patterns of early visual alteration across SZ and ASD including superior colliculus (SC) and pulvinar nucleus. In Experiment 1, simultaneous eye tracking and EEG were obtained from 91 individuals (35 NC, 20 ASD, 36 SZ). Fixation-related potential (FRP) was time-locked to fixation onset. In Experiment 2, fMRI during Guided Search was obtained from a partly overlapping sample of 71 individuals (27 NC, 25 ASD, 19 SZ). In behavioral analyses, SZ was associated with significantly prolonged search time (d=.74, p=.003), which was attributable primarily to reduced mean saccade amplitude, whereas ASD was associated with a small advantage (d=.35), which was not statistically significant. In EEG analyses, SZ was associated with reduced amplitude of the FRP P1 (lambda) response (d=1.15, p<.0001) relative to NC that remained significant following control for saccade size (p<.0001), but with normal task-related modulation of background alpha activity. In contrast, ASD was associated with normal FRP amplitude and larger alpha suppression (d=.83, p=.007) that was attributable to increased alpha levels during pre-task fixation (at matched pre-onset alpha levels, d=.14, p=.66). Within SZ, P1 correlated with the MCCB composite (r=.56, p=.001). Within ASD, ADOS-2 Communication correlated with P1 (r=.51, p=.024) and with the broadband change from pre-onset to search (r=-.51, p=.030). In fMRI, SZ was associated with correlated activation reductions in the Visual1 (Sidak p<.001) and Visual2 (Sidak p=.022) networks and SC (Sidak p=.019), whereas activation was unaffected in the Dorsal Attention and Frontoparietal networks, Frontal Eye Fields and pulvinar. In ASD, activation was increased in pulvinar (Sidak p[≤].038), but unaffected elsewhere. Cortical activation patterns associated with SC activation resembled those associated with P1 generation across groups. Overall, the findings support bottom-up disturbances of visual processing in schizophrenia. In autism, pre-onset alpha was higher and task-related suppression was larger.

papers.title: Attentional prioritization enhances the accessibility of neural representations during working memory maintenance
papers.abstract: Given the limited capacity of working memory (WM), prioritization is essential for efficient information processing. Whether prioritization acts primarily at encoding, or dynamically shapes representations during maintenance, is currently unclear. Here, we employed a delayed response task and compared prioritization conditions in which the testing order of items was either known in advance or not. Behaviorally, prioritization selectively reduced guess rates and had little effect on precision. Using multivariate pattern analysis, we decoded stimulus information from EEG voltage as an index of item specific representations, and used alpha power decoding as an index of internal attention. Prioritization did not alter decodable representations during encoding. During maintenance, however, prioritization enhanced both voltage-based decoding and alpha power-based decoding for the prioritized item. Mediation analyses further revealed an indirect association between alpha-based attentional signals and behavior via voltage-based representational strength, consistent with the idea that internal attention supports performance by maintaining prioritized representations in an accessible state.

papers.title: State-Dependent Organization of Microscale Functional Circuitry in Visual Cortex
papers.abstract: Directed functional connections between individual neurons, inferred from recorded activity, reflect information routing in cortex. Yet their organization across brain states and relation to synaptic connectivity remain poorly understood. Here, we present one of the largest single-neuron-resolution directed functional circuit maps, across about 45,000 neurons in four mouse visual areas. We inferred connections from deconvolved two-photon calcium activity with CITS, a causal-inference method designed for neural time series. In co-registered electron microscopy, CITS-inferred pairs were 3.0-fold more likely to be synaptically connected than other pairs. The map's organization aligned with synaptic connectivity at areal, laminar, and cell-type levels. In low and high pupil-linked arousal, the anterolateral area (AL) had the highest intra-areal density. The strongest inter-areal pathway linked AL with the rostrolateral area. This organization held in both states, yet mean connection strength was higher in high arousal in every scan, by 9.4% on average. Finally, stronger connections linked neurons with more similar stimulus-driven predictive performance in both states.

papers.title: Distinct neurophysiological signatures of guided visual search in schizophrenia and autism: Evidence from fixation-related potentials, alpha modulation, and functional MRI.

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.abstract: Long-term EEG is the main readout of rodent epilepsy models, and automated detectors are usually delivered as fixed models that a laboratory cannot adapt to its own animals. NED-Net is open-source software in which annotations, rule-based detections and model proposals share one file per recording, reviewed events train the next detector, and detection runs live during acquisition, so a detector can be refined while an experiment runs. A detector built in NED-Net on one kainate mouse cohort detected 64% of 221 video-adjudicated convulsive seizures in a second cohort as delivered, and 72% of its detections on held-out recordings were seizures. Retraining on annotations made in the app, a few seconds of review per event, raised recall to 88% at 74% precision. SeizyML, a published detector, reached similar recall with three times the detections and did not improve with the same annotations. A convulsive classifier removes non-seizures and enriches convulsive events.

papers.title: Towards an understanding of injury in aortic tissue prior to actual failure: quantification of mechanically induced collagen damage using collagen hybridizing peptides
papers.abstract: The development, validation, and optimization of endovascular aortic devices require quantitative assessment of tissue damage occurring during surgical interventions. Until now, this assessment--before complete failure--has been largely unfeasible for lack of a suitable methodology. Recently developed collagen hybridizing peptides (CHPs) allow selective detection of damage to collagen, the primary load-bearing constituent of the aortic wall. However, their application in large, mechanically loaded arteries has not yet been established. Therefore, we optimized an experimental workflow for large arteries that accounts for their energy-storage function and geometrical constraints; furthermore, we have characterized the tissue's autofluorescence and selected a suitable CHP fluorophore. Specimens from a single porcine aorta were examined using uniaxial tensile testing, histological analysis, fluorescence spectral analysis, confocal microscopy, and quantitative image analysis to present collagen damage as a function of tissue stretch. The workflow detected load-induced collagen damage before tissue failure, whereas histological evaluation showed no obvious load-induced disruption. Damage scores were comparable between the undeformed control and the specimen stretched by a factor of 1.2, while specimens stretched beyond 1.2 exhibited elevated scores. This pattern corresponded to higher complication rates with excessive stent oversizing. Furthermore, the proposed protocol can be adapted for ex vivo stent deployment experiments to compare collagen damage resulting from various aortic device designs and deployment conditions. Quantitative damage metrics could inform structurally motivated constitutive material models for computational simulations of endovascular interventions. Combined with histological and structural analyses, this workflow could also help link tissue composition--or organization--to individual susceptibility to damage.

papers.title: Expanded representation and function of PDF neurons in the mosquito circadian network
papers.abstract: Female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes can transmit pathogens when they bite humans, their preferred hosts, and this host-seeking drive is tightly gated by time of day. Daily rhythms depend on the molecular clock and communication among clock neurons, yet mosquito circadian network organization remains poorly understood. Using a mosquito-specific PERIOD antibody, we mapped the putative clock network of Aedes aegypti and found that neurons expressing the neuropeptide Pigment-Dispersing Factor (PDF) make up a much larger proportion of clock neurons compared to other insects, indicating a divergent network organization. PDF neurons are required for normal rhythms across insects, but whether their importance scales with their abundance in the network is unknown. We therefore tested the functional role of this expanded PDF neuron population in mosquitoes: we show that electrically silencing Aedes aegypti PDF neurons abolished the separation of daily activity into morning and evening peaks and led to misaligned clock protein rhythms across circadian neurons, even under entraining light-dark cycles. Thus, in a network built around an unusually large PDF population, PDF neuron activity plays an outsized role in behavioral timing and network synchrony.

papers.title: Prolonged loss of D1 receptor signaling promotes maladaptive plasticity of direct pathway striatal projection neurons
papers.abstract: As Parkinson's disease (PD) progresses and nigrostriatal dopamine (DA) neuron degeneration worsens, DA replacement therapies shift from restoring motor function to evoking dyskinesia. How disease progression mediates this transition remains poorly understood. Here, we optimized a 6-hydroxydopamine (6OHDA) model that reliably generates multiple severities of DA axon denervation within the striatum of individual mice. We identify a critical denervation threshold at which direct-pathway striatal projection neurons (dSPNs), which are key drivers of dyskinesia become pathologically hyperresponsive to DA. Using slice electrophysiology, we establish that denervation-induced increase in intrinsic excitability is insufficient to explain the aberrant response of dSPNs to DA. We further demonstrate using genetic and chemogenetic manipulations that prolonged loss of D1 receptor signaling drives the pathological transformation of dSPNs cell-autonomously, and that sustained Gs-coupled metabotropic receptor signaling in dSPNs is sufficient to both prevent and reverse it. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how PD progression renders striatal circuits vulnerable to DA-evoked motor complications and identify sustained signaling by Gs-coupled receptors as a potential avenue for preventing or reversing denervation-induced maladaptive striatal plasticity.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN: Identifying Phelan-McDermid-Like Electrophysiological Subtypes in Autism Using EEG and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript until a re-evaluation of the clinical data is completed. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.
